details.label: Summary
details.text: Strong to severe thunderstorms may materialize between 02-05 UTC across northern Illinois into northern Indiana. These storms will pose a risk of large to very large hail and severe gusts. Trends will be monitored, and watch issuance may be needed

details.label: Discussion
details.text: The northwestern edge of the cold pool associated with the earlier passage of an MCS is becoming increasingly diffuse across northern IL based on recently surface observations with temperature warming back into the upper 70s and briefly into the 80s before the onset of nocturnal cooling. Aloft, westerly 700-500 mb flow has advected steep lapse rates eastward back into the region, which were well sampled by the recent DVN and ILN 00 UTC RAOBs. As a result, the thermodynamic environment is steadily destabilizing and becoming increasingly supportive of intense convection. (These soundings also sampled extreme buoyancy between 4000-5000 J/kg MLCAPE and weak inhibition around -50 J/kg.) Over the past few hours, a subtle disturbance has been tracked across IA, evident by weak mid-level ascent. This feature has been supporting weak attempts at convection across southern MN and western WI, and will likely promote additional attempts within the destabilizing air mass across far eastern IA into northern IL later this evening. Latest guidance suggests that convective initiation is likely between 02-05 UTC, and will likely be focused along and north of the residual outflow boundary. Initially discrete to semi-discrete cells may mature into supercells before storm interactions within the zone of ascent promote clustering and upscale growth. Large to very large hail will be possible given the ample buoyancy and around 40 knots of effective shear if initially discrete modes can be adequately sustained. Strong to severe winds also appear possible given the shallow nature of the residual cold pool across northern IL. details.label: Summary
details.text: Very large hail and severe gusts remain likely this evening with several ongoing supercells

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Multiple intense supercells are present this evening across southwest ND and western SD. The 00Z observed sounding from UNR showed around 3500 J/kg of MLCAPE present to support these ongoing supercells, along with favorable deep layer shear of 45+ kt. Current expectations are that a threat for very large hail will continue this evening given the mainly discrete mode, presence of steep mid-level lapse rates, and favorable westerly shear vectors. The threat for severe gusts may also increase this evening, especially with an ongoing HP supercell transitioning to a small but intense bowing cluster with RFD surge evident in Butte/Meade Counties in western SD. This activity may tend to develop east-southeastward this evening into a very unstable airmass into parts of central SD, with 75+ mph gusts possible on an isolated basis. With Severe Thunderstorm Watch 569 in western SD scheduled to expire at 02Z, either a new watch or extension in time will likely be required within the next hour
